assumptions: Correction cell rings represent physical source spaces with horizontal floor/ceiling boundaries.
Contacts describe adjacency, not traversability or EnergyPlus surface pairing.
Only explicit openings are represented; absent observations do not establish a solid wall.
Source boundary identity follows cell identity and ring order; topology edits need identity migration.

Plan coordinate convention: x=0 West, x=15 East, y=0 South (min Y), y=8 North (max Y) -- confirmed by matching elevation window/door spacing to plan dimension chains: North_view.png bottom band (3 windows, 1240/2400/2660/2400/2660/2400/1240) matches the plan's top-of-image office row (now F1_N1/N2/N3 at y=[5,8]); South_view.png bottom band (entry door at 3440mm offset + 3 windows) matches the plan's bottom-of-image lounge row (now F1_S1/S2/S3 at y=[0,3], with entry door D_F1_S1_ext at y=0). The seed had these two rows swapped in Y (and consequently mislabeled window facades N/S) relative to this evidence; corrected via a y-axis reflect.

Uniform wall abstraction: exterior/partition wall thickness not individually modeled; rooms defined on a centerline grid (bays at x=0/5/7.5/10/11.25/15, y=0/3/5/8) derived from the dimension strings, reconciling to the 15.0 x 8.0 m envelope.
Floor-to-floor heights (F1=3.0 m, F2=3.6 m, total 6.6 m) taken directly from all four elevation drawings; F2 elevations use absolute world Z (z_floor=3.0).
Window sill/height per elevation dimension chains: F1 South/North row windows sill 1.0/h1.6m; East/West and all F2 windows sill1.0/h1.8m.
Interior door heights standardized to 2.1 m (not dimensioned on plan); F1 South entrance and West corridor exterior doors set to 2.4 m based on elevation glazing proportions.
Room F1_S1 small secondary window (South facade near entrance) has no explicit dimension string; size/position (0.7m wide, sill1.8m) is an inferred placeholder.

Redundant paired door leaves at shared partitions (F1 N/S rows, F2 M1/M2, and F2 O1/O2 & O3/O4) are each modeled as two separate corridor-facing doors (one per room), matching the two-arc pattern visible at every such partition in the drawings, rather than as a single direct room-to-room opening.

No door was modeled between F2 offices O2 and O3: zoomed inspection of that partition shows a plain continuous wall with no arc marks, unlike the O1/O2 and O3/O4 partitions which each show two corridor-facing arcs.

corrections.reason: North_view.png elevation matches the plan's top-of-image row (offices N1/N2/N3: 3-window spacing 1240/2400/2660/2400/2660/2400/1240 aligns with dimensioned office windows), and South_view.png matches the plan's bottom-of-image row (lounges S1/S2/S3 + entrance door at 3440mm offset, matching plan's 540+900+2000=3440mm entrance position). Since the model convention defines y=8 as North and y=0 as South, the top-of-image offices must be at high-y (North) and bottom-of-image lounges at low-y (South) -- the seed had these inverted (offices placed at y=[0,3], lounges at y=[5,8]), contradicted by the elevation evidence citations already embedded in the seed's own source_refs (W_F1_N1 cites North_view.png but was labeled facade South; W_F1_S1 cites South_view.png but was labeled facade North). Reflecting on y corrects the geometry to match elevation evidence while preserving all room/opening identities and connectivity.

Zoomed inspection of 2f_view.png at the O1/O2 partition shows a T-shaped partition wall with two separate door arcs both hinging from the corridor wall (y=3 line), one swinging into O1 and one swinging into O2 (matching the already-modeled D_F2_O2_C nearby). There is no opening through the vertical partition itself connecting O1 to O2 directly -- the partition is a continuous double-line wall. Reclassified this opening as O1's second corridor door rather than a direct O1-O2 connection.
